problem.statement: Distilled Intent Documents drifted into prose with the fields a reviewer wants collapsed or unrendered, while the site advertising them explained the product in words nobody could see running.
user_asks: "There is a lot of verbosity in the output and I would like to keep the output very simple and point wise as the developer persona wants to know the info in less time. How do we ensure that ? Shall we add a tool that makes the entire intent document terse before submitting ?"

"Actually this should apply to all fields including the Overview, what and why fields. Also, I feel, how the ask evolved may not be a very good output in the intent document as a reviewer is usually not interested in how the ask evolved and rather what choices were considered if applicable. What do you think ?"
"If a constraint shaped design, it should be part of the things tried or considered right ?"
"Cap evolution — ≤ 3 entries, ≤ 20 words, emerged_during_session only. I would say, lets remove the evolution altogether"

"I think we need to ensure that the reviewer has a strict command to keep things within budget like a non negotiable system prompt. Lets not do that enforcement. It is not needed. What is needed is to change the way."
"Budget can vary from commit to commit. What we are enforcing is the style."
"I dont like the non negotiable budget. Non negotiable is the style"
"Mention that to the author as well when it is answering reviewer's questions."
"Do we need to fix anything here ?"
"Its okay. Just publish it from this branch itself so that I can view the latest intent file through the new way."
"I think we did not commit the intent document at all"

"Lets redesign the UI to be more informative and talk about the usefulness of this mcp server and the github action. Lets keep it professional. Also, add blogs section and make it for each release so far. Keep it to the point and mention the fix and rationale. Use git to find it out."
"this is not needed in the releases page.. looks like a robot doing it."
"It is okay but not as per actual dev sides. Shall we introduce a more sci fi feel but keep it very subtle ?"
"I dont quite like the UI still, its boring. can we make it easy to view and something exciting. No emojis though as that smells AI,"

"Also, I see that there is a lot of real estate in the viewer but it is not utlilized. Can we do one thing. Can we create separate views for mobile and desktop and make sure to utilize entire screen for desktop and change it to fit for mobile ?"
"There is an agent working on the data. Fix the UI"

trials.what: Token budgets via the Anthropic `count_tokens` API.

adopted.summary:
- States the points style as non-negotiable in the reviewer role, the author role and the guide.
- Deletes `problem.evolution` from schema, types, both renderers, SPEC.md and the example.
- Routes user constraints to `trials` or `requirements` instead of narrative.
- Renders requirements and rejected alternatives without a fold, in the PR body and the viewer.
- Rebuilds the landing page around a live demo of the viewer, adds a `#/blog` release-notes route.
- Gives the viewer a full-width desktop shell and a real mobile navigation strip.
- Adds an instrument-panel design register and records its limits in DESIGN.md.
adopted.rationale:
- Style is stated as non-negotiable; bullet count is left to the size of the change.
- The rule is repeated in both role definitions and the guide, so no client sees only half of it.
- Corpus measurement set the target, not taste: `why` went 12 words to 96 on an unchanged guide.
- Bullets were already universal, so the fix had to reach inside the bullet.
- The guide's escape clause is deleted, because a cap beside it always loses.
- `adopted.rationale` gets its own rule, being where leftover prose collects.
- The rationale rule is prompt-side with no gate; the next document is the test.
- `evolution` is deleted rather than deprecated, so nothing can re-adopt it.
- Renderers flip in the same commit: a terser field still loses behind a fold.
- The demo runs the viewer's own `renderHunk`, so the page cannot advertise a viewer it lacks.
- The design register is held to three devices, keeping "subtle" from drifting.
- Full width goes only to code-bearing views; prose keeps a reading measure.
- Both concurrent sessions ship as one commit, at the user's explicit choice.

tour.title: Remove `problem.evolution` from the format
tour.what:
- Deletes `evolution` from the JSON schema, the `Problem` TypeScript interface, SPEC.md and `example.json`.
- Drops the "How the ask evolved" block from `renderMarkdown` and from the viewer overview.
- Keeps `problem.origin`; nothing replaces the narrative.
tour.why:
- The user's position: reviewers want the choices considered, not the play-by-play.
- The one thing the field carried that mattered — a user constraint — was already in `requirements` with a `source`.
- One committed document held 271 words of narrative under `origin: stated_upfront`.
- Eight self-authored documents were rewritten in place, no migration and no deprecation window.
tour.attention: `problem` is `additionalProperties: false` and the 0.1 schema was republished in place — any third-party document with the field now hard-fails, with no version bump signalling it.

tour.title: Bring requirements and rejected alternatives out of the folds
tour.what:
- Renders `approach.requirements` in the PR description for the first time.
- Replaces the `<details>` fold around trials with a "Considered and rejected" heading in both markdown paths.
- Swaps the viewer's `disclosure()` for `subsection()`, so neither section needs a click.
- Records the reasoning in the `renderPrDescription` doc comment.
tour.why:
- The surfaces were inverted: narrative expanded and top-level, trials collapsed, requirements absent from the PR body.
- Trials are not thin — 4-6 entries and 123-420 words in six of eight documents.
- `requirements` had `source` filled on 100% of entries in all eight documents.
- No reviewer-behaviour data exists; the case rests on the corpus and the user's stated preference.
tour.attention: PR body length with trials inline was never measured and no cap exists.

tour.title: Points as the non-negotiable style in the reviewer prompt and the guide
tour.what:
- Adds a "Non-negotiable: the style" section at the head of the reviewer role.
- Names the fields that are one point by nature — `problem.statement`, `tour[].attention`, `impact_if_wrong`, `requirements[].source`.
- Rewrites tour `why` guidance as points and converts the worked example to match.
- Deletes the guide clause licensing reasoning written "in full" as "the last thing to cut".
tour.why:
- Measured drift over eight documents on an unchanged guide: `why` averages 12 -> 23 -> 66 -> 96 words, total 15KB -> 51KB.
- The bullet rule already held in 11 of 11 stops; the bloat had moved inside the bullets.
- A cap next to the escape clause loses to the escape clause.
- The user rejected numbers three times, so style is the only thing stated as absolute.
tour.attention: the prompt now carries no number at all — check that "how many points" is genuinely decidable from the text.

tour.title: Give `adopted.rationale` a rule of its own
tour.what:
- Declares `adopted.rationale` a list, one point per reason the change has its shape.
- Adds a routing test: a point about an alternative is a `trials` entry, not a rationale point.
- States explicitly that it is not where leftover prose goes when the other fields are done.
- Mirrors the same rule into `guide.ts` beside the per-alternative rule for `trials`.
tour.why:
- Measured on the first document written under the points prompt: `why` converted 11 of 11 stops and `what` fell to 12 words per point, while rationale stayed one 179-word paragraph.
- Predicted when the caps were dropped: form constrains the unit, so a field with no unit stays a blob.
- Cause diagnosed as wording — rationale was named only negatively, which read as the place prose lives.
- Agent found it and argued for it; the user authorised with "Lets fix adopted rationale".
- The rule postdates `4b08d42`, whose rationale was the 179-word paragraph that prompted it.
tour.attention: a one-line prompt change with no gate behind it — the only evidence it takes is the next document's rationale.

tour.title: Route user constraints instead of narrating them
tour.what:
- `questions.md` now says the plan narrative is not a field; only `problem.origin` comes out of it.
- `reviewer.md` gains the routing test — a constraint that killed a candidate is a `trial`, one that only bounded the work is a `requirement` with the user in `source`.
- `guide.ts` states the same routing.
tour.why:
- The closeRun constraint is the worked case: narrative in `evolution`, sourced entry in `requirements`.
- The author still reconstructs how the ask evolved — deliberately kept as input to the interview, not output to the document.
- Without a destination, removing `evolution` would have lost real constraints.
tour.attention: the guide still asks the author for the ask's evolution — intentional asymmetry, not a leftover.

tour.title: The author role answers in points too
tour.what:
- Replaces "Answer, do not narrate" with "Answer in points", one point per fact.
- Adds "Never trade a fact for brevity" — terse is the shape of a point, not a limit on how many.
- Changes the relay instruction from replying in prose to replying in the same points.
tour.why:
- The user asked for the rule to reach the author as well.
- Whatever arrives as a paragraph the reviewer must compress, and compression is where restatement enters.
- The author is the only role that read the session, so an omitted point is unrecoverable.
tour.attention: the two roles are now given opposite instincts — select vs recall; check the text says which is which.

tour.title: Landing page rebuilt around the product
tour.what:
- Rewrites the hero and merges "Two installs" and "Get started" into one `Install` section, each part ending in its own action.
- Adds `siteHeader`/`siteFooter` shared by the landing page, the release notes and the viewer routes.
- Adds `richHtml`, a minimal inline-markup renderer for authored copy, injected via the `html:` prop.
- States the second install is a GitHub App, not an Action.
tour.why:
- The old page described a product nobody could see.
- The Action was retired in commit `70f0c3f`, so the copy contradicts the user's ask on purpose.
- The two install sections were the same section written twice.
tour.attention: `richHtml`'s link rule does not restrict the URL scheme and its output goes to an `html:` sink — safe only while every input is a literal in this file.

tour.title: The live demo panel
tour.what:
- Adds `renderDemo`, `paintDemo`, `startDemo`, `stopDemo` and a `DEMO` constant — a four-stop tour advancing on a 6s dwell.
- Renders the demo diff with `renderHunk`, the viewer's own function.
- Pauses on hover, stops permanently on click, and skips animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Forces a reflow between `width:0` and `width:100%` so the dwell bar actually transitions.
tour.why:
- The panel exists so the page shows the viewer instead of describing it.
- The progress bar was dead after the first stop: rAF runs before style recalc, so the two writes coalesced into no change.
- The interval leak across routes was anticipated and then verified absent, not observed.
- `DEMO` is hand-transcribed from `example.json` — no import, no test, and the diff string was re-edited three times to fit a 468px line box.
tour.attention: the header comment claims the demo cannot go stale, but only `renderHunk` is shared — the document text and diff are a copy, and stop T1's anchor claims 38 lines against an 8-line hunk.

tour.title: Release notes as a route, with 13 written entries
tour.what:
- Parses `#/blog` and `#/blog/<version>` in the same SPA and scrolls to top on every route change.
- Adds `renderBlogIndex`, `renderPost`, `releaseRow`, prev/next links and a compare link per release.
- Adds a 13-entry `RELEASES` constant, v0.2.1 through v1.0.0, each stating what broke, what was done and why.
- Surfaces the three newest on the landing page.
tour.why:
- Written this session from `git tag` and commit-message bodies; no changelog file existed to lift from.
- The user cut the index framing — "looks like a robot doing it" — so the eyebrow, headline and standards paragraph were deleted.
- Post bodies are a small block DSL (`h`, `ul`, `code`, `note`, plain string) rather than markdown.
tour.attention: the figures — 234,337 -> 15,622, "124 unit tests", "17 of 23 recorded trials" — are transcribed from commit bodies and were never re-derived.

tour.title: Full-width desktop shell and a mobile navigation strip
tour.what:
- Replaces the fixed `max-w-prose` main with `.shell`, capped at 120rem, and aligns the header to it.
- Gives code-bearing views the whole canvas (`.view-wide`); `submit` keeps a reading measure.
- Adds `.railbar`, a scrolling chip strip below `md`, plus `goStop` shared by rail and strip.
- Splits a walkthrough stop into sticky prose and a diff column, and Verification into two columns.
- Hides the coverage tag below `sm` and `@me` below `md`, moving the coverage figure into the chip strip.
tour.why:
- Diffs scrolled horizontally inside 648px with roughly 1000px empty; a stop is now 416px prose plus 1096px diff at 1552px.
- Below `md` the rail was hidden outright, so there was no way to reach a stop at all.
- The header shedding came from a failed first pass: at 390px the toggle sat 60px off-screen with 29px of overflow.
- Prose views deliberately keep a measure rather than stretching to 1900px.
tour.attention: the header's `z-10` -> `z-20` bump is unexplained in either session — read it as making room for the sticky railbar and confirm nothing else stacks between them.

tour.title: Overview in two measured columns
tour.what:
- Splits `renderOverview` into `left` (problem, out of scope, approach, diagrams, walkthrough button) and `right` (assumptions, open questions).
- Adds `.ov-split`: 32rem and 34rem tracks, centred as a pair, only at `xl`.
- Renames `section()`'s heading class to `.section-h`.
tour.why:
- Assumption cards ran 120+ characters per line at 1920 in the old single column; now 57-71.
- The track widths come from a measured 6.81px character advance, after three sizing attempts failed.
- `xl` is a space judgement, because the 288px rail has to be paid for first.
tour.attention: below `xl` the split collapses and assumptions fall after the Start-walkthrough button — never checked at md/lg, and it inverts "assumptions are the reviewer's front page".

tour.title: Instrument register: mono labels, section tick, masthead grid
tour.what:
- Makes `.eyebrow` and `.tag` mono at micro size and adds `.ordinal` for `01`/`02` numbering.
- Adds a 20px accent tick at the head of every `.section-h` rule.
- Adds `--grid-line` per palette and `.grid-field`, a 28px hairline grid masked on both axes, behind mastheads only.
- Records the three-device budget, the non-goals and the entry-point rule in DESIGN.md.
tour.why:
- The user asked for "a more sci fi feel but keep it very subtle", then chose "instrument panel" and "everything, viewer included".
- The three-device budget is the agent's own guard against future drift, not a user constraint.
- Grid alphas were set by eye per theme; the ΔL* figures are an after-the-fact check by a browser agent, not the input.
- The grid marks a page's entry point, so Verification deliberately has none.
tour.attention: `mask-composite: intersect` was never checked for browser support — without it the grid loses its fade.

tour.title: Mermaid re-themes with the page
tour.what:
- Replaces the one-shot `__mmInit` latch with `__mmTheme`, re-initialising mermaid whenever the theme changes.
- Adds `rerenderCurrent`, which redraws whichever of the three routes is live and restores scroll position.
- Points the theme toggle at `rerenderCurrent` instead of `render`.
tour.why:
- Pre-existing defect found during a dark-theme pass: diagram labels rendered #333 on near-black at 1.35:1, now 10.91:1.
- Re-init works because `render()` rebuilds the `<pre>` from source, so `mermaid.run`'s `:not([data-processed])` matches fresh nodes.
- The header is now shared by three routes, so the toggle can no longer assume the PR view is live.
- `rerenderCurrent` is also where `stopDemo()` fires, so a theme flip cannot orphan the demo interval.
tour.attention: toggle the theme on the landing page and on a release post, not only on a PR — that is the path the old code got wrong.

tour.title: Regenerated stylesheet
tour.why:
- Build artifact of `npm run build:css -w @review-assist/viewer`, not a hand edit.
- Must be committed in step with its sources or the shipped CSS lags them.
